about: 10CL016 per-register FF control bits (offline, Quartus builds of xdev design ffe2: with dffeas primitives). Cells relative to the LAB: frame = LUT frame 0 of LE N0 + 11, byte = low LUT byte of LE N0 + offset, plane = LE N0's LUT plane. sync_enable[i] (frame +11): set iff the register of LE i uses the LAB's synchronous clear/load (the same bit for sclr and sload, additive 15/15 each; LAB-wide bits choose clear vs load). aclr_enable[i] (frame +10): set iff it uses the LAB's asynchronous-clear line (additive 15/15, identical at X10Y10 and X22Y8). ena_line_select[i]: selects which of the LAB's two clock-enable lines the register of LE i uses; Quartus always keeps the lowest-numbered register on line 0, so the bit for LEs 0, 4, 8, 12 was not observed (null). Identical at X10Y10, X22Y8, X30Y20 for LEs 0-3 (16/16 combinations each); LEs 4-15 from X10Y10 only. Driving the LAB-wide lines needs routing bits, not mapped here. Not tested on silicon. ena_line_select_predicted: the 12 observed select bits sit in exactly the aclr_enable byte columns (frame +11 instead of +10), so the 4 unobserved ones are predicted there.
